children: Micron Technology Inc. (MU, Financials), the U.S. producer of memory chips that supplies high-bandwidth memory for standard artificial intelligence systems, has produced the kind of rise investors often dream of. Shares are up around 662% in the last year. And now the hard part comes.

Micron's progress has been supported by staggering numbers. For the fiscal third quarter, revenue was $41.46 billion, roughly a 346% increase on a year-over-year basis, with non-GAAP earnings of $25.11 per share. Gross margin of 84.9% (Company record).

AI is handling a lot of the grunt work. High-bandwidth memory is becoming crucial for advanced AI accelerators, especially those based on Nvidia CPUs. Micron also has long-term client contracts that provide greater visibility into future demand and price.
The company plans to report revenue of approximately $50 billion and earnings of $31 a share in the fourth quarter. Those figures explain the rally. They set expectations, too.
Micron is valued at $979.34 in a 24/7 Wall St. model, just below its latest price of $1,000.26, and its bull case might reach $1,347 if next-generation HBM4E accelerates quicker than predicted.
Micron no longer needs to convince investors AI memory demand is real. It has to demonstrate that it can create enough demand to support what the stock already anticipates is coming next.

title: Micron's 662% Rally Just Created a Problem Wall Street Cannot Ignore
